g.text: largest observed
lead: +17
shipped default
grace = 25
lead_years
Accepted matches
lead_years = certification year - NPI first-seen year. Positive means the NPI existed BEFORE the certification,
which is the suspicious direction. Negative is the normal career order: an RN enumerates before she certifies.
View clipped at -25; 583 further-negative rows (to -54) fall outside it and are never flagged by a one-sided rule.
B. The default grace sits above every value in the data
default grace = 25
flags 0 records
Grace period (years an NPI may precede certification)
Flagged (of 10,878 assessable)
Accepted matches called implausibly early, as the grace period tightens. These are candidate false positives
the name rules had no way to see -- not confirmed errors.
C. What a stricter grace period would actually flag
Reads the frozen crosswalk and the NPPES panel. first-seen is a BOUND, not a date: the panel opens in 2007 and NPPES began enumerating in 2006.
This is the VALIDATION half of D17 only. The SEPARATION half -- whether the signal breaks quarantined ties, and how many pools it would EMPTY in doing so --
requires artifacts/linkage_candidate_audit.csv with a populated first_year column, which the committed audit does not yet have.
Source: artifacts/amcb_npi_linkage_FROZEN.csv + midwife_panel.csv
The matcher blocks on names and taxonomy only: certification_date appears zero times in match_amcb_to_npi.R. This measures what a temporal
comparison would add, over matches ALREADY ACCEPTED. Nothing in the published linkage is changed by it.
What the unused temporal signal would buy (D17)
